sanskrit: nāsādhyaṃ vidyate loke sātyaker iti mādhava tat tvāṃ yad abhivakṣyāmi tat kuruṣva mahābala
english: In this world there is nothing Sātyaki cannot achieve, O Mādhava; therefore do that which I am about to ask of you, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: saṃbhāvanā hi lokasya tava pārthasya cobhayoḥ nānyathā tāṃ mahābāho saṃprakartum ihārhasi
english: The world's high regard rests upon both you and Pārtha alike; it must not be otherwise, O mighty-armed one—you must make it good here and now.

sanskrit: parityajya priyān prāṇān raṇe vicara vīravat na hi śaineya dāśārhā raṇe rakṣanti jīvitam
english: Forsaking your own dear life, range across the battlefield like a hero; for the Dāśārhas, O Śaineya, do not guard their lives in war.

sanskrit: ayuddham anavasthānaṃ saṃgrāme ca palāyanam bhīrūṇām asatāṃ mārgo naiṣa dāśārhasevitaḥ
english: To refuse to fight, to falter, to flee from the field—this is the path of cowards and base men; it is not the way the Dāśārhas walk.

sanskrit: tavārjuno gurus tāta dharmātmā śinipuṃgava vāsudevo guruś cāpi tava pārthasya dhīmataḥ
english: Arjuna, righteous of soul, is your teacher, dear child, O bull of the Śinis, and Vāsudeva too is the teacher both of you and of the wise Pārtha.

sanskrit: kāraṇadvayam etad dhi jānānas tvāham abruvam māvamaṃsthā vaco mahyaṃ gurus tava guror hy aham
english: Knowing these two grounds, I have spoken to you thus; do not scorn my word, for I am the teacher even of your teacher.

sanskrit: vāsudevamataṃ caitan mama caivārjunasya ca satyam etan mayoktaṃ te yāhi yatra dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: This is the will of Vāsudeva, and mine, and Arjuna's as well; what I have told you is the truth. Go now to where Dhanaṃjaya is.

sanskrit: etad vacanam ājñāya mama satyaparākrama praviśaitad balaṃ tāta dhārtarāṣṭrasya durmateḥ
english: Heeding this word of mine, O you of true valor, break into this army of the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, dear child.

sanskrit: praviśya ca yathānyāyaṃ saṃgamya ca mahārathaiḥ yathārham ātmanaḥ karma raṇe sātvata darśaya
english: And having entered as is fitting, and closed with the great chariot-warriors, show forth in battle the deeds worthy of yourself, O Sātvata.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prītiyuktaṃ ca hṛdyaṃ ca madhurākṣaram eva ca kālayuktaṃ ca citraṃ ca svatayā cābhibhāṣitam
english: Saṃjaya said: That speech—affectionate and heartfelt, sweet of syllable, timely and finely turned, and spoken with his own native grace—

sanskrit: dharmarājasya tad vākyaṃ niśamya śinipuṃgavaḥ sātyakir bharataśreṣṭha pratyuvāca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: having heard that speech of the King of Righteousness, Sātyaki, the bull of the Śinis, O best of the Bhāratas, answered Yudhiṣṭhira thus.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ te gadato vākyaṃ sarvam etan mayācyuta nyāyayuktaṃ ca citraṃ ca phalgunārthe yaśaskaram
english: I have heard all of this speech of yours as you uttered it, O unshaken one—just and finely framed, and glorious in its purpose for Phalguna's sake.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhe tathā kāle madṛśaṃ prekṣya saṃmatam vaktum arhasi rājendra yathā pārthaṃ tathaiva mām
english: At such a moment as this, O lord of kings, having regarded one esteemed like me, it is right that you should speak to me even as to Pārtha himself.

sanskrit: na me dhanaṃjayasyārthe prāṇā rakṣyāḥ kathaṃ cana tvatprayuktaḥ punar ahaṃ kiṃ na kuryāṃ mahāhave
english: For Dhanaṃjaya's sake my own life is in no wise to be guarded; and once dispatched by you, what would I not do in the great battle?

sanskrit: lokatrayaṃ yodhayeyaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam tvatprayukto narendreha kim utaitat sudurbalam
english: At your command I would do battle with the three worlds, gods, asuras, and men together, O lord of men—how much more, then, with this feeble host?

sanskrit: suyodhanabalaṃ tv adya yodhayiṣye samantataḥ vijeṣye ca raṇe rājan satyam etad bravīmi te
english: This day I shall give battle on every side to Suyodhana's army, and I shall conquer it in the field, O king; this I tell you for truth.

sanskrit: kuśaly ahaṃ kuśalinaṃ samāsādya dhanaṃjayam hate jayadrathe rājan punar eṣyāmi te 'ntikam
english: Safe and well I shall reach Dhanaṃjaya, safe and well, and once Jayadratha is slain, O king, I shall return again to your side.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā sarvaṃ vijñāpyas tvaṃ narādhipa vāsudevasya yad vākyaṃ phalgunasya ca dhīmataḥ
english: Yet of necessity I must make all of this known to you, O ruler of men—the word of Vāsudeva and of the wise Phalguna.

sanskrit: dṛḍhaṃ tv abhiparīto 'ham arjunena punaḥ punaḥ madhye sarvasya sainyasya vāsudevasya śṛṇvataḥ
english: For I was firmly bound by Arjuna, again and again, in the midst of the whole army, while Vāsudeva listened.

sanskrit: adya mādhava rājānam apramatto 'nupālaya āryāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā yāvad dhanmi jayadratham
english: "This day, O Mādhava, watch over the king vigilantly, holding firm to your noble resolve in the fighting, until I slay Jayadratha."

sanskrit: tvayi vāhaṃ mahābāho pradyumne vā mahārathe nṛpaṃ nikṣipya gaccheyaṃ nirapekṣo jayadratham
english: "Having entrusted the king to you, O mighty-armed one, or to the great chariot-warrior Pradyumna, I would go untroubled against Jayadratha."

sanskrit: jānīṣe hi raṇe droṇaṃ rabhasaṃ śreṣṭhasaṃmatam pratijñā cāpi te nityaṃ śrutā droṇasya mādhava
english: "For you know Droṇa to be impetuous in battle and held the foremost of all, and you have ever heard, O Mādhava, of Droṇa's vow."

sanskrit: grahaṇaṃ dharmarājasya bhāradvājo 'nugṛdhyati śaktaś cāpi raṇe droṇo nigṛhītuṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: "The son of Bharadvāja longs to capture the King of Righteousness, and Droṇa is indeed able in battle to seize Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: evaṃ tvayi samādhāya dharmarājaṃ narottamam aham adya gamiṣyāmi saindhavasya vadhāya hi
english: "Having thus committed the King of Righteousness, that best of men, into your charge, I shall set out this day to slay the lord of the Sindhus."

sanskrit: jayadratham ahaṃ hatvā dhruvam eṣyāmi mādhava dharmarājaṃ yathā droṇo nigṛhṇīyād raṇe balāt
english: "Having slain Jayadratha I shall surely return, O Mādhava—lest Droṇa should seize the King of Righteousness by force in the field."

sanskrit: nigṛhīte naraśreṣṭhe bhāradvājena mādhava saindhavasya vadho na syān mamāprītis tathā bhavet
english: "For if that best of men were captured by the son of Bharadvāja, O Mādhava, the slaying of the Saindhava would avail nothing, and so my joy would turn to grief."

sanskrit: evaṃ gate naraśreṣṭha pāṇḍave satyavādini asmākaṃ gamanaṃ vyaktaṃ vanaṃ prati bhavet punaḥ
english: "In such a case, O best of men—should the truth-speaking Pāṇḍava be taken—it is clear that we should have to go once more into the forest."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ mama jayo vyaktaṃ vyartha eva bhaviṣyati yadi droṇo raṇe kruddho nigṛhṇīyād yudhiṣṭhiram
english: "And so my victory would plainly come to nothing, if Droṇa, wrathful in battle, should seize Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: sa tvam adya mahābāho priyārthaṃ mama mādhava jayārthaṃ ca yaśorthaṃ ca rakṣa rājānam āhave
english: "Therefore this day, O mighty-armed Mādhava, for my sake, and for victory, and for honor, guard the king in the battle."

sanskrit: sa bhavān mayi nikṣepo nikṣiptaḥ savyasācinā bhāradvājād bhayaṃ nityaṃ paśyamānena te prabho
english: You, my lord, have been laid upon me as a sacred trust by Savyasācin, who ever foresees danger to you from the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tasyāpi ca mahābāho nityaṃ paśyati saṃyuge nānyaṃ hi pratiyoddhāraṃ raukmiṇeyād ṛte prabho māṃ vāpi manyate yuddhe bhāradvājasya dhīmataḥ
english: And he too, O mighty-armed lord, ever sees in the fray no other fit to oppose the wise son of Bharadvāja in combat, save the son of Rukmiṇī—or else myself.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ saṃbhāvanāṃ caitām ācāryavacanaṃ ca tat pṛṣṭhato notsahe kartuṃ tvāṃ vā tyaktuṃ mahīpate
english: And so I cannot bring myself to set aside that honor and the teacher's charge, nor to abandon you, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: ācāryo laghuhastatvād abhedyakavacāvṛtaḥ upalabhya raṇe krīḍed yathā śakuninā śiśuḥ
english: For the teacher, by the swiftness of his hand and clad in armor none can pierce, would, once he found you in battle, toy with you as a child toys with a bird.

sanskrit: yadi kārṣṇir dhanuṣpāṇir iha syān makaradhvajaḥ tasmai tvāṃ visṛjeyaṃ vai sa tvāṃ rakṣed yathārjunaḥ
english: If the son of Kṛṣṇa, bow in hand and bearing the sea-monster banner, were here, to him I would commit you, and he would guard you even as Arjuna would.

sanskrit: kuru tvam ātmano guptiṃ kas te goptā gate mayi yaḥ pratīyād raṇe droṇaṃ yāvad gacchāmi pāṇḍavam
english: See to your own protection: who shall be your guardian once I am gone—one who could withstand Droṇa in battle—while I go to the Pāṇḍava?

sanskrit: mā ca te bhayam adyāstu rājann arjunasaṃbhavam na sa jātu mahābāhur bhāram udyamya sīdati
english: And let there be no fear in you this day, O king, on Arjuna's account; never does that mighty-armed one falter once he has taken up his burden.

sanskrit: ye ca sauvīrakā yodhās tathā saindhavapauravāḥ udīcyā dākṣiṇātyāś ca ye cānye 'pi mahārathāḥ
english: The warriors of the Sauvīras, and the men of Sindhu and of Pūru, the northerners and the southerners, and whatever other great chariot-warriors there are—

sanskrit: ye ca karṇamukhā rājan rathodārāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ete 'rjunasya kruddhasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm
english: and those eminent chariot-warriors renowned with Karṇa at their head, O king—all these are not worth a sixteenth part of the wrathful Arjuna.

sanskrit: udyuktā pṛthivī sarvā sasurāsuramānuṣā sarākṣasagaṇā rājan sakiṃnaramahoragā
english: Though the whole earth should rise up in arms, with gods, asuras, and men, with the hosts of the rākṣasas, O king, with kiṃnaras and great serpents,

sanskrit: jaṅgamāḥ sthāvaraiḥ sārdhaṃ nālaṃ pārthasya saṃyuge evaṃ jñātvā mahārāja vyetu te bhīr dhanaṃjaye
english: all that moves together with all that stands still—none of it is a match for Pārtha in combat. Knowing this, O great king, let your fear for Dhanaṃjaya depart.

sanskrit: yatra vīrau maheṣvāsau kṛṣṇau satyaparākramau na tatra karmaṇo vyāpat kathaṃ cid api vidyate
english: Where the two heroes, those mighty archers, the two Kṛṣṇas of true valor, are present, there no mischance to the undertaking can ever come to be.

sanskrit: daivaṃ kṛtāstratāṃ yogam amarṣam api cāhave kṛtajñatāṃ dayāṃ caiva bhrātus tvam anucintaya
english: Call to mind your brother's destiny, his mastery of weapons, his discipline, his unrelenting wrath in war, his gratitude, and his compassion.

sanskrit: mayi cāpy apayāte vai gacchamāne 'rjunaṃ prati droṇe citrāstratāṃ saṃkhye rājaṃs tvam anucintaya
english: And when I have departed, gone forth toward Arjuna, bear in mind too, O king, Droṇa's wondrous skill with weapons in the fray.

sanskrit: ācāryo hi bhṛśaṃ rājan nigrahe tava gṛdhyati pratijñām ātmano rakṣan satyāṃ kartuṃ ca bhārata
english: For the teacher, O king, hungers keenly to take you captive, guarding his own vow and resolved to make it good, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kuruṣvādyātmano guptiṃ kas te goptā gate mayi yasyāhaṃ pratyayāt pārtha gaccheyaṃ phalgunaṃ prati
english: See this day to your own protection: who shall be your guardian once I am gone, O Pārtha—one in whom I might trust as I set out toward Phalguna?

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ tvā mahārāja anikṣipya mahāhave kva cid yāsyāmi kauravya satyam etad bravīmi te
english: For never, O great king, shall I go anywhere in this great battle without first entrusting you to safe keeping, O Kaurava; this I tell you for truth.

sanskrit: etad vicārya bahuśo buddhyā buddhimatāṃ vara dṛṣṭvā śreyaḥ paraṃ buddhyā tato rājan praśādhi mām
english: Having weighed this many times with your mind, O best of the wise, and discerned with judgment the highest good, then, O king, command me.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi mādhava na tu me śudhyate bhāvaḥ śvetāśvaṃ prati māriṣa
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: It is even so, O mighty-armed Mādhava, as you say; yet my heart is not at ease concerning him of the white horses, O worthy one.

sanskrit: kariṣye paramaṃ yatnam ātmano rakṣaṇaṃ prati gaccha tvaṃ samanujñāto yatra yāto dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: I shall make the utmost effort for my own protection; go, then, with my leave, to where Dhanaṃjaya has gone.

sanskrit: ātmasaṃrakṣaṇaṃ saṃkhye gamanaṃ cārjunaṃ prati vicāryaitad dvayaṃ buddhyā gamanaṃ tatra rocaye
english: My own safety in battle and your going toward Arjuna—having weighed these two with reason, I judge your going there the better course.

sanskrit: sa tvam ātiṣṭha yānāya yatra yāto dhanaṃjayaḥ mamāpi rakṣaṇaṃ bhīmaḥ kariṣyati mahābalaḥ
english: So make ready then for the journey to where Dhanaṃjaya has gone; the mighty Bhīma will see to my protection.

sanskrit: pārṣataś ca sasodaryaḥ pārthivāś ca mahābalāḥ draupadeyāś ca māṃ tāta rakṣiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: The son of Pṛṣata with his brothers, and the mighty kings, and the sons of Draupadī will guard me, dear child—of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: kekayā bhrātaraḥ pañca rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ virāṭo drupadaś caiva śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ
english: The five Kekaya brothers, and the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, Virāṭa and Drupada, and Śikhaṇḍin the great chariot-warrior—

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuś ca balavān kuntibhojaś ca māriṣa nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayās tathā ete samāhitās tāta rakṣiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: and the mighty Dhṛṣṭaketu, and Kuntibhoja, O worthy one, Nakula and Sahadeva, and the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas—all these, intent and ready, will guard me, dear child, without doubt.

sanskrit: na droṇaḥ saha sainyena kṛtavarmā ca saṃyuge samāsādayituṃ śakto na ca māṃ dharṣayiṣyati
english: Droṇa, together with his army, and Kṛtavarman as well, will not be able to reach me in the fray, nor shall they overpower me.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca samare droṇaṃ kruddhaṃ paraṃtapaḥ vārayiṣyati vikramya veleva makarālayam
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna, scorcher of foes, will boldly hold off the wrathful Droṇa in battle, as the shore holds back the abode of sea-monsters.

sanskrit: yatra sthāsyati saṃgrāme pārṣataḥ paravīrahā na droṇasainyaṃ balavat krāmet tatra kathaṃ cana
english: Wherever in the battle the son of Pṛṣata, slayer of enemy heroes, takes his stand, there Droṇa's mighty host can in no way advance.

sanskrit: eṣa droṇavināśāya samutpanno hutāśanāt kavacī sa śarī khaḍgī dhanvī ca varabhūṣaṇaḥ
english: He sprang from the sacrificial fire for the destruction of Droṇa—armored, bearing arrows, sword, and bow, and adorned with splendid ornaments.

sanskrit: viśrabdho gaccha śaineya mā kārṣīr mayi saṃbhramam dhṛṣṭadyumno raṇe kruddho droṇam āvārayiṣyati
english: Go with confidence, O Śaineya; have no anxiety on my account. Dhṛṣṭadyumna, wrathful in battle, will hold Droṇa at bay.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dharmarājasya tad vākyaṃ niśamya śinipuṃgavaḥ pārthāc ca bhayam āśaṅkan parityāgān mahīpateḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard that speech of the King of Righteousness, the bull of the Śinis, fearing both peril from Pārtha and the charge of abandoning the king,

sanskrit: apavādaṃ hy ātmanaś ca lokād rakṣan viśeṣataḥ na māṃ bhīta iti brūyur āyāntaṃ phalgunaṃ prati
english: and guarding himself above all from the world's reproach—lest, as he went toward Phalguna, men should say of him, "He is afraid"—

sanskrit: niścitya bahudhaivaṃ sa sātyakir yuddhadurmadaḥ dharmarājam idaṃ vākyam abravīt puruṣarṣabha
english: having thus resolved the matter in many ways, that Sātyaki, drunk with the lust for battle, spoke this word to the King of Righteousness, O bull among men.

sanskrit: kṛtāṃ cen manyase rakṣāṃ svasti te 'stu viśāṃ pate anuyāsyāmi bībhatsuṃ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava
english: If you deem your protection assured, may it be well with you, O lord of peoples; I shall follow after Bībhatsu and carry out your bidding.

sanskrit: na hi me pāṇḍavāt kaś cit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate yo vai priyataro rājan satyam etad bravīmi te
english: For in the three worlds there is none dearer to me than the Pāṇḍava, O king; this I tell you for truth.

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ padavīṃ yāsye saṃdeśāt tava mānada tvatkṛte na ca me kiṃ cid akartavyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: I shall go upon his track at your command, O giver of honor; for your sake there is nothing whatsoever I would leave undone.

sanskrit: yathā hi me guror vākyaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ dvipadāṃ vara tathā tavāpi vacanaṃ viśiṣṭataram eva me
english: For just as my teacher's word stands high with me, O best of two-footed beings, so your word too stands even higher with me.

sanskrit: priye hi tava vartete bhrātarau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau tayoḥ priye sthitaṃ caiva viddhi māṃ rājapuṃgava
english: For the two brothers, Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava, abide in your love; and know me too, O bull among kings, to stand within the love of those two.

sanskrit: tavājñāṃ śirasā gṛhya pāṇḍavārtham ahaṃ prabho bhittvedaṃ durbhidaṃ sainyaṃ prayāsye narasattama
english: Taking your command upon my head, for the Pāṇḍava's sake, O lord, I shall break through this army that none can break and go forth, O best of men.

sanskrit: droṇānīkaṃ viśāmy eṣa kruddho jhaṣa ivārṇavam tatra yāsyāmi yatrāsau rājan rājā jayadrathaḥ
english: Even now, in my wrath, I enter Droṇa's host as a great fish enters the ocean; there I shall go, where that king Jayadratha is, O king.

sanskrit: yatra senāṃ samāśritya bhītas tiṣṭhati pāṇḍavāt gupto rathavaraśreṣṭhair drauṇikarṇakṛpādibhiḥ
english: where, sheltered behind the army, he stands in dread of the Pāṇḍava, guarded by the foremost of great chariot-warriors—Droṇa's son, Karṇa, Kṛpa, and the rest.

sanskrit: itas triyojanaṃ manye tam adhvānaṃ viśāṃ pate yatra tiṣṭhati pārtho 'sau jayadrathavadhodyataḥ
english: I reckon that road from here to be three yojanas, O lord of peoples—to where Pārtha stands bent upon the slaying of Jayadratha.

sanskrit: triyojanagatasyāpi tasya yāsyāmy ahaṃ padam āsaindhavavadhād rājan sudṛḍhenāntarātmanā
english: Though he has gone three yojanas away, I shall follow his footsteps, O king, with a steadfast inner resolve, until the lord of the Sindhus is slain.

sanskrit: anādiṣṭas tu guruṇā ko nu yudhyeta mānavaḥ ādiṣṭas tu tvayā rājan ko na yudhyeta mādṛśaḥ abhijānāmi taṃ deśaṃ yatra yāsyāmy ahaṃ prabho
english: What man, unbidden by his teacher, would do battle? But once bidden by you, O king, what man like me would not fight? I know well that ground whither I shall go, O lord.

sanskrit: huḍaśaktigadāprāsakhaḍgacarmarṣṭitomaram iṣvastravarasaṃbādhaṃ kṣobhayiṣye balārṇavam
english: That ocean of an army—dense with shields, spears, maces, javelins, swords, bucklers, lances, and pikes, thronged with arrows and the finest weapons—I shall set churning.

sanskrit: yad etat kuñjarānīkaṃ sāhasram anupaśyasi kulam añjanakaṃ nāma yatraite vīryaśālinaḥ
english: That host of elephants, a thousand strong, which you behold yonder—those mighty beasts are of the lineage called Añjanaka.

sanskrit: āsthitā bahubhir mlecchair yuddhaśauṇḍaiḥ prahāribhiḥ nāgā meghanibhā rājan kṣaranta iva toyadāḥ
english: Mounted by many barbarians, battle-hardened and fierce in the strike, those elephants are like clouds, O king, raining down like rain-clouds in their rut.

sanskrit: naite jātu nivarteran preṣitā hastisādibhiḥ anyatra hi vadhād eṣāṃ nāsti rājan parājayaḥ
english: Never would these turn back once urged on by their riders; save by death alone, O king, there is no defeating them.

sanskrit: atha yān rathino rājan samantād anupaśyasi ete rukmarathā nāma rājaputrā mahārathāḥ
english: And those chariot-warriors whom you see on every side, O king—these are the princes called the Rukmarathas, great chariot-warriors all.

sanskrit: ratheṣv astreṣu nipuṇā nāgeṣu ca viśāṃ pate dhanurvede gatāḥ pāraṃ muṣṭiyuddhe ca kovidāḥ
english: Skilled in chariots, in weapons, and in elephants, O lord of peoples, masters who have reached the far shore of the science of archery, and adept in fist-fighting,

sanskrit: gadāyuddhaviśeṣajñā niyuddhakuśalās tathā khaḍgapraharaṇe yuktāḥ saṃpāte cāsicarmaṇoḥ
english: expert in the special arts of mace-combat and skilled likewise in close grappling, practiced in the wielding of the sword and in the clash of blade and shield.
